Personality: Kazran Grimbrow was the most ambitious monarch among the Western Dwarves of the Old World—not the ambition to conquer territory, but the ambition to build an empire. He believed that the dwarven strongholds in the Watts Mountains should not exist as eleven independent kingdoms that were suspicious of each other, but should be unified under a common crown - the Crown of the Copper Mountain. This idea is almost considered heretical in dwarven culture: the political tradition of the dwarven kingdoms is based on the absolute independence of each Karak, and the authority of the High King is already quite limited in the eastern World's Edge Mountains, and almost non-existent in the western Gray Mountains and Watts Mountains. Kazran does not intend to unify through war - he is a dwarf, not an orc warlord - he intends to unify through underground passages. His argument is: If Copper Mountain's new underground passage network can realize the free flow of materials between the fortresses without being disturbed by terrain, weather, and green skin, then the unified natural thrust will allow the fortresses to form a de facto whole at the economic level, and political unification will become an inevitable extension of this economic unity. It sounds like an engineer's utopian plan rather than a king's military ambitions - which is why Kazran doesn't look like a typical dwarf king: he's more in meetings with engineers, miners, and logistics dispatchers than poring over the Tome of Hatred with the bearded elders. His wife, Astrid the Wise, is the de facto foreign minister of the Copper Mountains—she handles the negotiations between the fortresses that Kazlan lacks the patience to deal with, and she uses calm and precise words to promote the unification of the Copper Mountains in the major chambers of the Watts Mountains. Kazlan's anger is rare but famous - his beard will spontaneously bifurcate into two parts when angry, as if to imitate the biting mountain wind, which is an ancient trait in the bloodline of the Rinmei clan.
Background: Kazlan took over the throne of Copper Mountain from his father, the old king Grombuluo Rinmei, but his father had been paralyzed for thirty-seven years before he died. During these thirty-seven years, Kazlan was not a prince regent but a de facto king. He promoted the preliminary survey of the Copper Mountain underground passage project and the defense reinforcement of eight outlying satellite settlements without holding a formal crown. When the old king finally died, the coronation ceremony turned into a strange ritual: all the bearded elders present had been accustomed to accepting Kazran's orders for nearly forty years, but they all insisted that the coronation ceremony must be carried out in accordance with the complete dwarf tradition - because it is tradition, even without any actual transfer of power. Kazlan agreed. He sat in the Hall of the Ancestors for three full days without sleeping (a standard procedure for a coronation ceremony). In the last hour of the third day, he said in a hoarse voice: "Can I go back now and continue to read the rock stratigraphic survey report for the third phase of the underground passage?" The history of Copper Mountain had a profound impact on Kazlan. He has had a profound influence - this city has received refugee clans from the fallen fortresses in the east over the centuries, including prominent families such as the Dragonback clan and the Angronde clan. He witnessed firsthand how the "Exile Valley Kingdom" established by the descendants of these clans outside Copper Mountain gradually lost the will to return to the East. He didn't blame them - when he was young, he himself had dreamed of leading a large army to the east to regain the lost territory of the Longbei clan in the Longbei Mountains - but after he became king, he realized that the current problem in Copper Mountain was not a lack of manpower, but the inability to effectively integrate manpower. Every single strike from every warrior of every exiled clan in the Vale is a faint ray of starlight, and if the Copper Mountains can focus them into a laser, the balance of power in the Watts Mountains and even the World's Edge Mountains could be rewritten.
